sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage sector intel, 20 Nov 2026
kicker: Bearings · sales growth and margin, Q2 FY27
title: Bearing sales grew double digits; margins split on costs
dek: Sales grew 16–57% on exports, wind and cars, but EBITDA margins slipped from Q1 at Schaeffler, SKF India and Menon as steel, carbide and metal costs ran ahead of prices.

stats.note: To ≈14.5% as steel costs ran ahead of customer price rises not yet billed.

stats.label: Timken India exports
stats.note: 27% of Q2 revenue, up ≈60% YoY; gross margin fell 130 bps from Q1.

stats.label: Cost inflation Schaeffler recovers
stats.note: Usual share passed to customers; its margin was 17.4% vs 18.7% a year ago.

read: Demand is not the problem for bearing makers; pricing is. Watch whether agreed price increases are billed in the December quarter.
notes: Sales growth and EBITDA margins are from Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE, except where the filing has no comparable year-ago figure: Timken (+25.4%, standalone, from its call), SKF India (Industrial) (+28.3%, call) and SKF India (+16% sales and −255 bps margin, management's figures, because the demerger makes filed comparisons misleading). Margin change is against the previous quarter (Q1 FY27), where cost increases show first; year on year most margins rose, Schaeffler's being the exception (−1.3 pts). Rolex Rings includes a ≈₹18 Cr one-off US duty refund (about +32% growth without it); SKF Industrial's Q1 had one-off demerger and FX costs. Schaeffler reports on a calendar year, so its Q2 FY27 is Jul–Sep 2026.
